longForm.heroLead: Moisture testing shouldn't take hours. The Computrac® MAX 4000XL cuts loss-on-drying analysis down to minutes — up to 100x faster than a standard oven reference method, and 25% faster than other rapid LOD instruments on the market. The speed comes from a built-in lid fan that rapidly cools the heating chamber between tests. Less waiting, more samples through the door. Accuracy doesn't get traded away for speed. A 100-microgram resolution balance delivers repeatable, defensible results, run after run. The enclosure is all-steel. The heating element is nickel chromium. Built for the lab bench and the production floor alike. What it measures: moisture and solids content, across food, pharmaceutical, plastics, and chemical applications. What it stores: 250 test programs, 1,000 results, 100 graphs — all on the instrument. What it shows: real-time moisture curves and rate-of-loss data, live, on a large color display.

sections.tabSummary: Why the lid fan is the whole speed story
sections.title: Rapid Cooling and Throughput
sections.description: Why the lid fan is the real story behind the 25% figure.
body: Loss-on-drying testing has a bottleneck most people don't think about: the chamber has to cool before the next sample goes in. Every minute spent cooling is a minute the instrument isn't testing.
MAX 4000XL's built-in lid fan solves that directly. It cools the heating chamber fast, and Brookfield states the result plainly: 25% faster throughput than other rapid loss-on-drying instruments.
That's not a marginal gain. Across a full shift of testing, 25% is the difference between finishing the queue and carrying samples into tomorrow.

sections.tabSummary: Free moisture, bound moisture, one test sequence
sections.eyebrow: Multistage Testing and Flexible Ending Criteria
sections.title: Multistage Testing and Flexible Ending Criteria
sections.description: Free moisture. Bound moisture. One test.
body: Not all moisture behaves the same way. Some evaporates fast and easily — free moisture. Some is chemically bound to the material and needs a different temperature, a different endpoint, to release.

MAX 4000XL links multiple test stages into one sequence. Temperature, ending criteria, and timing can all change between segments — so a single run captures both free and bound moisture without manual intervention between stages.
User-adjustable ending criteria go further: the test stops when your material says it's done, not when a generic default says so.

longForm.heroLead: Thermogravimetric analyzers do this job well. They also cost a lot more than most labs need to spend. Computrac® MAX 5000XL delivers the features typically found in a TGA, at a fraction of the price. The heater reaches up to 600°C, hot enough to run both loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition tests on the same sample. That means moisture, solids, and ash content, all from one measurement, not three separate tests on three separate instruments. Results come back in half an hour or less. One-button operation runs the whole test, no intermediate weighing, no manual cooling steps in between. The enclosure is cast aluminum, built for the production floor as much as the lab bench. What it replaces: the need for a separate, expensive TGA for many applications. What it adds: a self-cleaning oven cycle, 45 minutes at 550°C, that keeps maintenance simple. Where it fits: plastics, pharmaceuticals, foods, and biomass materials.

sections.tabSummary: Why 600°C changes what this solution can measure
sections.title: A Cost-Effective Alternative to TGA
sections.description: Why 600°C changes the value proposition against a thermogravimetric analyzer.
body: Thermogravimetric analyzers measure moisture, solids, and ash by precisely tracking mass change as temperature rises. They're the reference standard for this kind of testing. They also carry a price tag that puts them out of reach for many labs that only occasionally need that level of capability.

MAX 5000XL closes that gap. A heater reaching 600°C runs both loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition tests, which is what lets one sample yield moisture, solids, and ash data without switching equipment. Brookfield states this plainly: features typically found in more expensive thermogravimetric analyzers, delivered in a solution built for a fraction of the cost.

Construction backs that up. The cast aluminum enclosure and high-temperature heater are built specifically to withstand demanding environments while still delivering lab-quality data, whether the solution sits on a bench or on a production floor.

sections.tabSummary: Why RH-sensor technology changes what gets measured
sections.title: Moisture-Specific Detection, Not Weight Loss
sections.description: Why RH-sensor technology changes what gets measured.
body: Loss-on-drying and loss-on-ignition methods measure how much mass a sample loses when heated, then assume the loss is moisture. That assumption breaks down when a sample contains other volatile compounds. The instrument can't tell the difference, and the result reads high.

Vapor Pro XL sidesteps that problem entirely. RH-sensor technology detects moisture specifically, not total mass loss, which means the result reflects actual water content even in samples where other volatiles are present. Sensitivity reaches 10 micrograms of water, low enough to determine moisture content as low as 10ppm, a level weight-loss methods typically can't resolve reliably.

sections.description: What zero reagents actually removes from the Karl Fischer titration workflow.
body: Karl Fischer titration is accurate, and it comes with real overhead. Reagents that require careful handling and disposal. Glassware that needs cleaning and replacement. Titrant that has to be standardized and tracked. None of that goes away on its own.

Vapor Pro XL removes it. Zero chemical reagents, with results Brookfield states correlate well with Karl Fischer titration. The workflow becomes load a sealed vial, run the test, read the result, without the reagent purchasing, handling protocols, or waste disposal that KF titration carries as a matter of course.
